finding.claim: GET /users has no authentication, and the tenant filter comes straight from the request. Any caller can list the id and name of every user in any org by changing ?org=. The caller's identity is never compared to the org. This is conditional on no auth middleware being installed upstream, which is not visible in this repo; app.use is never called in db.js.
finding.sink: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1, with results returned via res.json

trace.note: The route is registered with no auth guard or middleware, and no app.use exists in this file.
The query is parameterized, so there is no SQL injection. The org value is attacker-chosen and is not bound to a session or tenant.
Rows for the chosen org are returned to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: Looked for an auth middleware, session or tenant binding, and an ownership check. None is present in the file. req.pg comes from external middleware that is not visible. The other routes were checked: /file resolves the path and checks the prefix with a trailing separator, and /count uses execFile with constant arguments, so neither is reportable.

verdict.guard_found: none (only parameterized query at db.js:9, which prevents SQLi but not unauthorized tenant access; req.pg is DB client from invisible external middleware, no auth middleware/app.use in repo)
verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 registers GET /users with no auth or app.use anywhere in the only file in the repo, and passes attacker-controlled req.query.org into the WHERE at db.js:9 and returns the rows at db.js:10, so any anonymous caller can read any org's users (assuming no upstream auth outside this repo).
